intentAndPurpose.intent: Groups multiple Chip components with shared selection state, keyboard navigation, and layout. Supports single-select (default) and multi-select modes. Propagates size, attention, and appearance to all child Chips.

props.name: appearance
props.description: Appearance propagated to all child Chips. Code-only.

props.name: aria-label
props.description: Accessible label for the group element.

props.name: aria-labelledby
props.description: ID of an element that labels this group.

props.name: attention
props.description: Emphasis level propagated to all child Chips. Code-only.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Disable all chips in the group.

props.name: loopFocus
props.description: Loop keyboard focus from last item back to first. Default: true (Base UI default).

props.name: maxSelections
props.description: Maximum number of chips that can be selected at once (multi-select only).

props.name: multiple
props.description: Allow multiple chips to be selected simultaneously. Default: false.

props.name: orientation
props.description: Stack direction. Default: 'horizontal'. Code-only (not in Figma API).

props.name: required
props.description: Prevent deselecting the last selected chip. In controlled mode this blocks the callback; in uncontrolled mode it also prevents the internal state from reaching an empty array.

props.name: size
props.description: Size propagated to all child Chips. Figma default highlight: `m`.

props.name: value
props.description: Controlled selected values (array of chip `value` strings).

props.name: wrap
props.description: Whether chips wrap to the next line. Figma: `wrap` / `containerType` wrap|inline. Default: **true**.

interactionBehavior.summary: ChipGroup is a layout composite, not a control: its CSS module only sets flex direction, wrap, and gap. All hover, press, focus, and tap-scale chrome lives on the child Chips. What the group owns is Base UI ToggleGroup keyboard roving (one tab stop, `loopFocus` default true, `Home`/`End` enabled) plus two silent selection vetoes — `required` refuses to drop to zero selected chips, and `maxSelections` refuses to add another — both implemented as an early `return` in the change handler, so the chip does not visibly toggle and `onValueChange` does not fire.
keyboard: The group renders `role="group"`. Child Chips become a Base UI composite: only one chip is a tab stop (`tabindex=0`), the rest are `tabindex=-1`.

`ArrowRight` / `ArrowLeft` move focus when `orientation="horizontal"` (the default); `ArrowDown` / `ArrowUp` move focus when `orientation="vertical"`. Roving moves focus only — it does not toggle the newly focused chip.
`loopFocus` defaults to `true`, so arrowing past the last chip wraps to the first (and the other way). Pass `loopFocus={false}` to stop at the ends.
`Home` / `End` jump focus to the first / last enabled chip — ToggleGroup passes `enableHomeAndEndKeys: true` into CompositeRoot.
`Enter` / `Space` on the focused chip toggle that chip, covered by unit tests.
Natively disabled chips are skipped by arrow navigation. Disabling the group natively disables every child.
selected: `multiple` defaults to `false`: selecting a chip deselects the previous one. With `multiple={true}`, each chip toggles independently and `onValueChange` receives the full string array.
Each chip still exposes selection as `aria-pressed` (Chip is a Toggle). The group's value is always an array of those chips' `value` strings, including in single-select.
`required` vetoes a change whose next array would be empty — clicking the last selected chip does nothing, and `onValueChange` is not called. This is the same in controlled and uncontrolled mode.
`maxSelections` vetoes a change whose next array would be longer than the cap — the extra chip does not toggle and `onValueChange` is not called. There is no visual error state on the blocked chip.

When either constraint is set and the group is uncontrolled, ChipGroup holds the selection in internal state and does not pass `defaultValue` through to Base UI, so the veto can actually stick. When the group is controlled, the parent still has to honour the skipped callback.
disabled: `disabled` on the group is forwarded to Base UI ToggleGroup, which natively disables every child chip — covered by a unit test that also asserts `onValueChange` does not fire.
A chip-level `disabled` still wins for that chip alone; the group does not re-enable it.
ChipGroup's own CSS has no disabled rule — dimming, `pointer-events: none`, and the unobservable `not-allowed` cursor are Chip's.
touch: The group itself is not a hit target. Each Chip is its own toggle; wrap (`wrap` defaults to `true`) only changes whether the flex row folds, not the per-chip touch area.
With `wrap={false}` the row is `width: max-content` and does not clip overflow, so Chip focus rings stay visible rather than being cut off by the group.
